- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) and forecast is significantly above recent history, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.3) and forecast is below recent history, increase forecast by 5–10% to avoid underreaction.  
- If forecast peaks sharply after a spike in sentiment, reduce the peak by 10–15% to account for mean reversion.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days of history show strong upward momentum, forecast should not overshoot by more than 5% above the 18-day moving average.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, adjust forecast to align with the most recent sentiment trend, not the long-term average.  
- When sentiment is neutral (0.0–0.3) and forecast is drifting, apply a slight downward bias to avoid false momentum.  
- For forecasts with high volatility in sentiment, reduce forecast variance by 15–20% to reflect reduced confidence.
